before-talking-to-captain-pudi-with-leve.npc: Sorry, can't talk to ye right now. Busy with paperwork. If ye need anythin', talk t' Captain Pudi over by the dock.

after-talking-to-captain-pudi-with-level.npc: What can I do for ye? I be quite busy with paperwork.

options.text: I heard about your ship, can you tell me what happened?

steps.player: I heard about your ship. Can you tell me what happened?

steps.npc: Aye, I can tell ye what happened.
We be out on our fortnightly fishin' trip, I was doin' me normal work. Setting up the nets, swabbing the deck and the like.
'Twas a good hawl t' start, plenty of manta ray and snappers. But we would be movin' on the next day to our deep sea fishin' spot.
'Twas nothin' but smooth sailin' to our deep sea spot near Karamja, but on the way I noticed more debris in the water than usual.

steps.player: What kind of debris? Was it ship debris?

steps.npc: Aye, 'twas. Most of the time, it be nets or items people throw off ships that they don't need. This had me worried a bit.
There was a lack of fish in the water, 'twas kind of... eerie.
The next day, Koanee changed the ship's course, but that be because of a storm on the horizon.
But the storm seemed t' be... following us. As if it had a mind of its own.
The wind started a blowin' and the fog started a showin', huge waves crashing against the boat.
The ship started fallin' apart. I rushed to the cook's quarters and found 'im layin' on the floor with a plank over 'im.
I brought 'im up to the top deck and tied 'im to a piece of loose wood. I did the same t' the Skipper and Navigator.

steps.player: Oh my, that's awful! You're very lucky you didn't get hit.

steps.npc: Aye, it be lucky indeed. But that not be the end of it. As the ship finished sinking, I balanced out the wood so we did not slip.
In the distance I saw glowing eyes and a large monster sorta thing in the fog movin' t'wards us.
But all of a sudden, it vanished. I then had to keep us afloat 'till we made it t' shore by Al Kharid.
Pudi gathered us up and we went t' the Chancellor as soon as we could stand.
These ruins turned out t' be a great base to research the beast from undisturbed! Bit close to Menaphos though, aye?
That be the end of me story. Can I help ye with anything else?

options.text: A pirate doing paperwork, that's new.

steps.player: A pirate doing paperwork, that's new.

steps.npc: Let me guess, ye thought we be doin' nothing but pluderin' and pillagin'?

steps.player: Is that not what pirates do?

steps.npc: Ye be a funny one.

steps.player: Glad you can still smile after what happened.

steps.npc: I'm not goin' t' let one bit of bad luck keep me down.
Can I help ye with anything else?

options.text: Got any tips for fighting Tempoross?

steps.player: Got any tips for fighting Tempoross?

steps.npc: Tempoross can summon clouds that shoot lightnin'. They can cause fires that will block ye from movin' about as freely.
Ye best be ready to grab a bucket and douse the fire before it spreads!
Can I help ye with anythin' else?
Stay safe, ye hear?

using-items-on-her-damp-egg.player: Would you care for an egg in this difficult time?

steps.npc: Um... no, I don't want your damp egg, thanks...

steps.player: I'll take my eggs elsewhere then.

steps.npc: A damp egg? No thanks.

steps.player: I'll take my eggs elsewhere then.

steps.npc: I'd rather not. Thanks, though.

steps.player: I'll take my eggs elsewhere then.

using-items-on-her-egg.player: Would you care for an egg in this difficult time?

using-items-on-her-egg.npc: This is some comfort to be sure.
